text: Trust those only to some tried friend, more experienced than yourself, and who, being in a different walk of life from you, is not likely to become your rival; for I would not advise you to depend so much upon the heroic virtue of mankind, as to hope or believe that your competitor will ever be your friend, as to the object of that competition.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XCVII, to his son, London, December 19, Old Style 1749
